title: Nayantacawnick (Probable Fishers Island)
summary: Nayantacawnick is the island name Roger Williams used in 1637 while discussing the forced placement of captive Pequot families. Historical place-name sources interpret it as being opposite Niantic and identify Fishers Island as the most likely modern location, while also naming Plum Island as an alternative.
address_label: Fishers Island, Town of Southold, NY (probable broad identification)
map_geometry_source: Representative Fishers Island point based on the historical interpretation 'over against Niantic'; probable identification, with Plum Island retained as an alternative.
why_this_matters: Nayantacawnick preserves a seventeenth-century regional name while also documenting a proposal to confine Pequot families after war. Mapping the probable island makes that history visible, and retaining the uncertainty prevents a geographic inference from being presented as settled fact.
introduction_content: Roger Williams used Nayantacawnick in a 1637 letter about where captive Pequot families might be confined after the Pequot War. The surviving record establishes the name and its regional setting but does not provide a modern survey or boundary.
history_content: The name appears in a colonial proposal to separate and confine Pequot captives. It should therefore be read within the history of warfare, enslavement, family disruption, and forced dispersal rather than as a neutral island label.
translation_content: Tooker and Douglas-Lithgow interpreted the name as meaning over against Niantic. Both treated Fishers Island or Plum Island as possibilities. Fishers Island is the stronger geographic inference because it lies directly across the sound from Niantic, but the identification remains probable, not certain.
whereintheworld_content: The marker is a representative point on Fishers Island, the likeliest of two islands proposed by historical researchers. Plum Island remains an alternative identification, so the point does not claim a proven historic boundary or exact site.
